description: Finalize dependencies, documentation, and the offline test harness: pin requirements.txt for the Lambda layer, expand README.md with layer packaging / env vars / handler path / Function URL / checkpointer TTL / four-table schema, and add the pytest harness (conftest.py, pytest.ini, tests/) that makes the whole suite runnable offline. Depends on FEAT-001..003 (the tests reference those modules). handler.py and whatsapp_lambda.py stay untouched.
steps: Overwrite requirements.txt with pinned packages: fastapi==0.115.12, mangum==0.19.0, langgraph==0.2.76, langgraph-checkpoint==2.0.26, langchain-aws==0.2.19, langchain-core==0.3.63, pydantic==2.11.4, requests==2.32.3, boto3==1.35.99. Add a comment that boto3 is runtime-bundled (pinned only for local/tests) and must not ship in the layer. Keep moto+pytest in a separate dev note or requirements-dev.txt (not in the layer).

Add a README.md section 'LangGraph FastAPI agent Lambda' documenting: which packages go in the layer (everything except boto3); build steps (pip install -r requirements.txt -t python/ ; zip -r layer.zip python); all env vars (BEDROCK_MODEL_ID, USERS_TABLE_NAME, CHAT_HISTORY_TABLE_NAME, CHECKPOINTER_TABLE_NAME, MAPPING_TABLE_NAME, ORDER_API_ENDPOINT, ORDER_API_KEY optional, WHATSAPP_PHONE_NUMBER_ID, META_API_VERSION, AWS_REGION); the Lambda handler path app.lambda_handler; that the Function URL must be enabled and public; that the checkpointer table needs TTL enabled on expires_at; and the four tables with their key schemas (USERS PK user_id; CHAT_HISTORY PK conversation_id SK sk; CHECKPOINTER PK pk SK sk + TTL expires_at; MAPPING PK conversation_id). Note handler.py and whatsapp_lambda.py remain as reference and are not the deployed entry point.

Add pytest.ini (or pyproject [tool.pytest]) pointing at tests/, and conftest.py that sets all required env vars (table names, BEDROCK_MODEL_ID, ORDER_API_ENDPOINT, etc.) before imports, provides moto DynamoDB fixtures creating the four tables with the documented keys, and helpers to mock ChatBedrockConverse, requests.post, and the socialmessaging send. Ensure tests import the new modules after env is set.

Ensure tests/test_data.py, tests/test_checkpointer.py, tests/test_agent.py, tests/test_app.py (authored in FEAT-001..003) are collected and the full suite is green; add any missing cross-feature integration test (e.g. end-to-end run_agent authorized->interrupt->resume->POST using mocks).
acceptance_criteria: pip install -r requirements.txt resolves cleanly in a fresh Python 3.12 venv.
python -c "import app, agent, checkpointer, data, whatsapp" succeeds.
python -m pytest -q runs the entire suite green offline.
README documents layer packaging, all env vars, handler path app.lambda_handler, Function URL public, checkpointer TTL on expires_at, and the four table key schemas.
handler.py and whatsapp_lambda.py are unchanged (git diff shows no edits to them).
verification: python -m pip install -r requirements.txt  (clean Python 3.12 venv; resolves)
python -c "import app, agent, checkpointer, data, whatsapp"
findings:
Implemented and verified offline. All three verification commands pass: python import of app/agent/checkpointer/data/whatsapp succeeds; `pip install -r requirements.txt --dry-run` resolves cleanly on Python 3.12; `python -m pytest` is 24 passed (23 prior FEAT-001..003 + 1 new cross-feature integration test). handler.py and whatsapp_lambda.py are unchanged (git diff --stat empty).

requirements.txt: pinned to the versions actually installed and VERIFIED against (the langgraph 1.x line), NOT the context.json 0.2.x sketch. FEAT-001/002/003 all recorded that the code was built and verified against langgraph 1.1.3 / langgraph-checkpoint 4.0.0 / langchain-aws 1.4.1 / langchain-core 1.6.3 / fastapi 0.135.2 / mangum 0.19.0 / pydantic 2.12.5 / requests 2.32.5 / boto3 1.43.103. Pinning to 0.2.76 would contradict the one hard, testable acceptance criterion (clean resolve + green suite) since the modules use the v1 BaseCheckpointSaver/interrupt/Command APIs. The deviation is documented inline in requirements.txt and in the README 'Dependency versions' note. boto3 is pinned for local/tests with an explicit comment that it is runtime-bundled and must be excluded from the layer. pytest+moto moved to a new requirements-dev.txt (dev-only, not in layer); it does `-r requirements.txt` then adds pytest==9.1.1, moto==5.2.4.

README.md: added a 'LangGraph FastAPI agent Lambda' section (kept the original SNS->SQS reference content above it). Documents: module map; handler path app.lambda_handler and that it dispatches aws:sqs events to the SQS batch path and the rest to Mangum; Function URL must be enabled and public (auth NONE) with permissive CORS for the file:// test page; layer packaging (everything except boto3; pip install -t python/ ; remove boto3/botocore ; zip -r layer.zip python) and that the deploy zip carries only the .py files + test_page.html; full env-var table (BEDROCK_MODEL_ID, USERS/CHAT_HISTORY/CHECKPOINTER/MAPPING table names, ORDER_API_ENDPOINT, optional ORDER_API_KEY, WHATSAPP_PHONE_NUMBER_ID gating outbound sends, META_API_VERSION default v20.0, AWS_REGION default us-east-1); the four tables with key schemas (USERS PK user_id; CHAT_HISTORY PK conversation_id SK sk; CHECKPOINTER PK pk SK sk + TTL on expires_at; MAPPING PK conversation_id) and the TTL-on-expires_at requirement; and a note that handler.py/whatsapp_lambda.py are reference, not the deployed entry point.

pytest.ini + conftest.py already existed from FEAT-003's test-infra fix and already satisfy FEAT-004 (testpaths=tests; env vars seeded at conftest import time for collection-time imports, re-applied per test via the autouse _env monkeypatch fixture; moto `dynamodb` fixture creating the four tables with the documented keys). Extended conftest.py with shared, opt-in mock helpers requested by step 3: ScriptedLLM + `scripted_llm` factory (stand-in for tool-bound ChatBedrockConverse), `order_response`/`mock_requests_post` (requests.post -> {'workflow_id':'wf-777'}), and `mock_socialmessaging` (patches whatsapp.send_whatsapp_message). The pre-existing per-feature tests keep their own self-contained mocks and were left untouched.

New cross-feature integration test tests/test_integration.py: drives run_agent end-to-end against the REAL DynamoDBSaver (moto checkpointer table) and REAL data.* helpers (moto users/mapping/chat tables) with only the Bedrock LLM and requests.post mocked. Asserts: authorized id seeded in users table -> turn 1 pauses on the confirm interrupt with no POST and no mapping; the paused thread is persisted in the checkpointer table (get_state(...).next non-empty); resume 'yes' -> requests.post called once with conversation_id in the body and data.get_mapping returns {workflow_id: wf-777, user_id: u-123, whatsapp_number}. This is the first test exercising the checkpointer + data layers together through the graph (test_agent.py uses InMemorySaver and mocks data.*).

Did NOT edit handler.py, whatsapp_lambda.py, agent.py, app.py, data.py, checkpointer.py, whatsapp.py, or test_page.html.
